terms.comment: Lewis & Short: to bring, carry or convey a thing to a place. What the courier does: fasciculus allātus est, the parcel has been delivered.

evidence: Cic. Att. 8.5.2: fasciculum … velim cūrēs ad eum perferendum
M-O s.v. deliver (a letter), after Egger
terms.comment: Of a letter or a packet carried all the way to the one it is for.
In Lewis & Short only a late legal word, a carrying (Ulp.).
litterās reddere is the classical phrase for handing over a letter.

phrases.latin: tū fasciculum, quī est M’. Curiō īnscrīptus, velim cūrēs ad eum perferendum
phrases.english: please see that the packet addressed to Manius Curius gets to him

sources: Lewis & Short: affero · Lewis & Short: perfero · Lewis & Short: perlatio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 363.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. deliver (a letter).
